subject: SLA variance heatmap + cost decomposition: implementation ask
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2029-05-03T09:12:00Z
Subject: SLA variance heatmap + cost decomposition: ask

Team —

Quick ask from my side after a Beacon Health postmortem this morning. We keep seeing route-level SLA volatility (p95/p99 jumps) that lines up with cost spikes, but the Console today doesn't make it easy to correlate SLA variance with the underlying token-paths and cost buckets. Beacon is asking for a way to: 

- Visualize SLA variance by tenant/route over selectable windows (1h, 6h, 24h) as a heatmap so we can spot persistent problem slices.
- Break down per-tenant cost contribution by the highest-impact token-paths (e.g., long-chat tail, embedding-heavy flows) when a variance occurs.
- Export the decomposed view to CSV for finance/CS analysis.
- Pin a heatmap snapshot to route pages and link to the per-route trace list for quick triage.

I've attached a small sample CSV export from Beacon's tenant (sla-variance-sample.csv) and a mockup (heatmap-mockup.png) that illustrates the flow I have in mind. Also opening INF-1782 to track.

Acceptance criteria (initial):
- Heatmap UI available under Console -> Insights -> "SLA variance" with tenant and route filters.
- Clicking a heatmap cell shows top-10 token-paths by added cost and token count for that bucket.
- CSV export with columns: timestamp, tenant_id, route, p50/p95/p99, token-path-id, token-count, token-cost, call-count.
- Reasonable performance for 30 days of data for paid customers (degraded by sampling for very large accounts).

Ask: can Eng/Product estimate effort and decide whether this is an "Optimize" epic candidate for Q3? Beacon may push hard on this as part of renewal.

Attachments: sla-variance-sample.csv (text/csv), heatmap-mockup.png (image/png)

Thanks —
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Product Manager, Console & Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SLA variance heatmap + cost decomposition: ask

Thanks for the write-up, Rishi — this is very clear and I agree Beacon will want this surfaced. A couple quick clarifying questions before I scope: 

1) SLO buckets: do you want discrete buckets (e.g., 0-50ms, 50-200ms, 200-500ms, >500ms) or percentile-driven thresholds (p95/p99 cutoffs)? My preference is percentile-driven so it adjusts across route types, but discrete buckets are easier to surface in a heatmap.
2) Sampling: the mockup implies near-complete token-path attribution. For very large tenants we probably need to sample. What fidelity do CS/finance need in the CSV?
3) UX: can we reuse the existing "route compare" component (Marissa) or do we need a new tile?

Diego — can you ballpark an eng estimate (discovery + PoC + production) and call out any infra blockers (cardinality, precomputation jobs, new indexes)?

I can pull this into the Console backlog and write initial acceptance criteria once we align.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

On Fri, May 3, 2029 at 10:30 Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> 1) SLO buckets: do you want discrete buckets (e.g., 0-50ms, 50-200ms, 200-500ms, >500ms) or percentile-driven thresholds (p95/p99 cutoffs)?
> 2) Sampling: the mockup implies near-complete token-path attribution. For very large tenants we probably need to sample.
> 3) UX: can we reuse the existing "route compare" component (Marissa) or do we need a new tile?

Short answers up front: percentile-driven thresholds is preferred; sampling will be required for high-cardinality tenants; reusing route-compare would be ideal.

Estimate (very rough):
- Discovery + schema design: 5 eng-days (including one data infra sync).
- Backend prototype (precompute heatmap tiles for 24h windows): 10 eng-days.
- Frontend prototype (heatmap + drill pane + CSV export): 8 eng-days.
- Hardening + pagination + auth/scoping + perf tests: 7 eng-days.
Total: ~30 eng-days across FE/BE/infra (2-3 people over 4 weeks).

Technical concerns:
- Cardinality: token-path IDs explode for open chat sessions; we'll need a normalization step (hash token-paths by fingerprint + truncate depth) or a top-N by cost approach.
- Data latency: computing accurate p99 across heavy tenants requires either event aggregation streams (kafka-based) or an offline daily job; near-real-time heatmaps will be heuristics.
- Storage: to support 30-day windows with per-tenant drilldowns we should materialize aggregated tiles per tenant/route/timeslice (hourly) instead of cold scans.

Mitigation proposal: incremental rollout — build hourly precompute and heatmap UI that shows sampled/estimated results with a clear note; refine to exact counts for paid tiers. This will keep Beacon happy initially and avoid a large infra spike.

I'll create an infra spike ticket and tag it INF-1782 and link a proto branch by EOW. Can Product define the SLA buckets (percentile thresholds) and the CSV output columns we will lock to?

-Diego
Diego Fernandez
Engineering Lead, Observability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLA variance heatmap + cost decomposition: ask

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with what Beacon needs. Next steps I will drive: 

1) Product (me / Kim): finalize acceptance criteria and percentile buckets (p50/p95/p99 + anomaly band flag).
2) Engineering (Diego): spin up INF-1782 infra spike to validate hourly materialization and a sampling plan; prototype branch by 2029-05-10.
3) UX (Marissa): adapt route-compare into a heatmap tile and wire the drill pane; mockups due 2029-05-08.
4) CS/Account (cc external): I will share the sample CSV and mockup with Beacon and confirm whether they need sub-route token-path detail or top-N only.

Acceptance criteria (final draft):
- Heatmap tile in Console shows tenant/route axes and selectable time windows (1h/6h/24h/7d).
- Drill pane lists top-10 token-path fingerprints with token-count, token-cost, and call-count; CSV export matches the columns Rishi listed earlier.
- For large tenants we show an estimation badge and sampling rate in the CSV metadata.
- Infra spike demonstrates hourly materialization at scale for 10 high-volume tenants.

Marissa — can you add this to the Console backlog as a candidate Q3 "Optimize" epic and set a short grooming with Eng next week? I will reach out to Beacon to tell them we're starting a PoC.

Thanks all —
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
